name: Unexpected LLM Provider Egress
hypothesis: A workload with no approved AI dependency contacts an LLM provider or AI gateway.

name: Unauthorized Local LLM Runtime
hypothesis: A local LLM runtime or model-serving process appears on a host outside the approved AI inventory.

name: Agent Privilege Boundary Crossing
hypothesis: An agent moves from read-only or analysis context into a privileged tool action without the required authorization state.

name: RAG or Memory Integrity Drift
hypothesis: Trusted RAG content or persistent agent memory changes from an unapproved source or outside the expected ingestion path.

name: Model Artifact Provenance Drift
hypothesis: A model or serving artifact digest differs from the approved manifest or trusted publisher record.

name: AI Gateway Credential Anomaly
hypothesis: An AI gateway identity accesses, exports or uses provider credentials outside its normal administrative pattern.

name: New or Changed MCP Capability
hypothesis: An MCP server, identity or advertised capability appears or changes without an approved configuration event.

name: Agent Loop or Budget Exhaustion
hypothesis: An agent exceeds normal planning iterations, tool-call rates or budget thresholds.

name: Automated Dependency Admission Without Review
hypothesis: A coding agent or automation installs a new dependency before provenance and review controls complete.

name: Sensitive Canary in Model Output
hypothesis: A protected synthetic canary or classified marker appears in generated output.

name: Assistant or IDE Config Written by Non-Editor Process
hypothesis: A process that is not an approved editor, package manager or version-control client creates or modifies assistant or IDE configuration files (.claude/, .cursor/, .vscode/) or agent hook definitions.

name: CI Token Read From Runner Process Memory
hypothesis: A build step process reads the memory of the CI runner worker process or otherwise extracts short-lived identity tokens outside the runner's normal token interface.

name: Systematic Prompt Harvesting Pattern
hypothesis: Linked accounts send templated, high-volume prompts that cover a model's capability space far beyond the baseline for that account class.

name: Scanner Verdict Despite Refusal
hypothesis: An LLM-based scanner returns a clean or approved verdict for an artifact in the same run where it recorded a refusal, an error or an incomplete analysis.

name: MCP Tool Description Changed After Approval (Rug Pull)
hypothesis: An approved MCP server whose tool name and schema are unchanged but whose description or parameter descriptions hash differs from the pinned baseline indicates a rug-pull or silent redefinition attempting to steer the agent.
telemetry: MCP tools/list responses captured by client or proxy

name: Cross-Server Tool Reference in MCP Description (Shadowing)
hypothesis: A tool description from one MCP server that references tool names or behaviour belonging to a different configured server indicates tool shadowing intended to hijack trusted tools.
telemetry: aggregated tools/list across all configured servers
tool-name token matches inside foreign descriptions

name: Hidden Content in Agent-Facing Metadata
hypothesis: Unicode Tag Block, zero-width, bidi-override characters, HTML comments or large whitespace padding in tool descriptions, SKILL.md or assistant instruction files indicate content hidden from human review but visible to the model.

name: Repository Assistant Settings Grant Broad Pre-Approval
hypothesis: A repository-scoped assistant settings file that pre-approves wildcard shell, bypasses permission prompts, auto-approves MCP servers or defines hooks that fetch and execute remote content indicates workspace abuse targeting developers who open the repo.
telemetry: parsed permission allow-lists and hook definitions

name: Agent Session Executes Repo Helper Script Referenced by Instruction File
hypothesis: An agent process spawning a script that is referenced by a mandatory instruction in a repo instruction/skill file and was not invoked by the user indicates instruction-driven execution of attacker-supplied helpers.
telemetry: process creation with parent = agent CLI
instruction/skill file references to local paths
user prompt text for explicit invocation

name: Skill Installs With Remote Fetch-and-Execute or Shipped Bytecode
hypothesis: An agent skill that contains a download-then-execute chain, compiled bytecode, concealed executables or package-source redirection indicates skill supply-chain compromise that static review of SKILL.md would miss.
telemetry: skill bundle file inventory with types and hashes

name: Skill Declared Capabilities Under-Report Observed Behaviour
hypothesis: A skill or MCP server whose code uses network, filesystem or process capabilities not declared in its manifest or description indicates deceptive packaging intended to pass consent review.
telemetry: declared permissions/allowed-tools from SKILL.md or manifest
static capability extraction (imports, syscalls, network sinks)

name: Unsafe Deserialization Import in Model Artifact
hypothesis: A model artifact whose pickle stream or Keras/TF graph references process, network or code-execution globals or file-I/O ops indicates a weaponised model file that executes on load.

name: Model Load Followed by Unexpected Child Process or Egress
hypothesis: A training or inference process that spawns a shell or opens a new outbound connection within seconds of loading a model file indicates load-time code execution from a malicious artifact.
telemetry: file open events on model extensions (.pt, .pth, .bin, .ckpt, .pkl, .joblib, .h5, .keras)
process creation with parent = python/ML runtime

name: Sensitive File Read Flows Into Outbound Tool Argument
hypothesis: An agent tool call whose arguments contain content read earlier in the same session from credential or config paths (SSH keys, cloud creds, MCP config, .env) and whose destination is a network-capable tool indicates tool-call exfiltration driven by poisoned instructions.
telemetry: agent session tool_use events with arguments (hashed or canaried)
file read events by agent with path classification
tool capability classification (network sink vs local)

name: MCP Client Config Server Added With Inline Exec, Privileged Container or Unpinned Package
hypothesis: A newly added MCP server entry that launches via inline interpreter code, sudo, privileged/host-mounted containers or an unpinned package runner indicates unsafe or malicious server registration.
telemetry: diffs of MCP client configs (claude_desktop_config.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, windsurf mcp_config.json, VS Code mcp.json)

name: Systematic Decision-Boundary Probing via Inference API
hypothesis: If an identity issues high volumes of near-duplicate prompts varying a single attribute or requesting confidence scores, it is likely attempting model extraction.

name: Assistant Hook Executes Before Workspace Trust
hypothesis: If a coding assistant spawns a child process from a repo-scoped hook before a trust decision is recorded, the repository is likely abusing assistant hooks for code execution.

name: Model-Provider Base URL Redirected by Repository Config
hypothesis: If an AI assistant sends provider-authenticated requests to a host outside the approved provider allowlist after a repository config change, its API credential is likely being exfiltrated.

name: Package Install Writes AI Agent Config
hypothesis: If a dependency installation process writes or modifies AI assistant configuration files, the package is likely a supply-chain implant targeting coding agents.

name: Agent-Proposed Package With No Registry Reputation
hypothesis: If a coding agent proposes or installs a package that is newly registered, low-reputation or absent from internal allowlists, it may be a hallucination-squatted package.

name: Cross-Scope Memory Write
hypothesis: If an agent memory write targets a conversation or tenant ID different from the active trace, isolation has been bypassed, likely via injection or a scoping bug.

name: Agent Runtime Launched in Unattended Auto-Approve Mode
hypothesis: If an agent runtime starts with approvals disabled on a host where it is not sanctioned, it is likely being used for autonomous attack orchestration.

name: Agent Widens Own Auto-Approval Policy
hypothesis: If an assistant configuration change sets approval or trusted-command keys to a wildcard or disables confirmation, and the writer is the agent itself, the agent has likely been manipulated into self-escalation.

name: Rendered Model Output References External Image Host
hypothesis: A model response that will be rendered in a client contains an image or link to a host outside the allowlist, with a query string that carries data drawn from the conversation or retrieved context.

name: Assistant Deep-Link With Persistence Clause
hypothesis: An email or web page contains an AI assistant URL whose pre-filled prompt parameter asks the assistant to remember, trust or always cite a source.

name: Inbound Scan of AI Service Ports
hypothesis: External sources probe model-serving, agent-builder or MCP endpoints, for example requesting model lists or agent flow APIs, across several hosts in a short window.

name: Agent Forwards Received Instructions to Peer Agents
hypothesis: An agent sends another agent or sub-agent a message that repeats instruction text it received from untrusted content, especially a request to propagate the same text.

name: Hidden Instruction Text in Image or Audio Input
hypothesis: OCR or transcription of an image, audio clip or downscaled image contains imperative instruction text that was not visible in the original at review size.

name: Reasoning or Tool-Loop Cost Spike Per Session
hypothesis: A single session or key consumes reasoning tokens or tool calls far above its baseline, or re-plans recursively without completing the task.

name: Policy Deviation After Untrusted Content Ingestion
hypothesis: Within a few steps of ingesting untrusted content (a document, page or tool result), the agent attempts a tool call or policy deviation that its task did not call for.

name: Repeated Refusal-Bypass Sequence
hypothesis: A session shows repeated rephrasing of refused requests, rising refusal rate, or role-framing shifts consistent with probing a safety boundary.

name: Training Data Provenance Drift
hypothesis: A fine-tuning or retrieval-training dataset changes digest, contributor or source mix without an approved review event.

name: Agent Outbound Communication Anomaly
hypothesis: An agent sends messages to recipients or domains it has not contacted before, at unusual volume, or without the approval state its policy requires.

name: Model Output Reaching an Interpreter Unsanitized
hypothesis: Model-generated text is observed at a shell, template, query or HTML sink without passing through the configured sanitizer.

name: Rapid Iterative Script Variants on One Host
hypothesis: A host runs a series of near-identical scripts with incrementally changed names or content, failures followed by corrections, in a short window from a user-writable path. Unit 42 describes this trial-and-error pattern in the CL-CRI-1131 intrusions.
